title: Compatible-pair presentation of ideal-power numerators
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\iota:I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$ a monomorphism [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with $I$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], $F$ any $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $V$ affine. Set $R=\mathcal O_X(V)$ and $M=F(V)$. Let $g:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$ generate $\operatorname{im}(\iota(V))$, and let $k\geq0$ and $x_i\in M$ satisfy $g_j^k x_i=g_i^k x_j$ for all $i,j<t$. Put $n=tk+1$ and let $(P_n,j_n)$ be the recursive image power [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Then $P_n$ is quasi-coherent, $\operatorname{im}(j_n(V))\subseteq(g_i^k\mid i<t)$, and there are an $R$-module $E$ and $R$-linear maps $p:E\to P_n(V)$ and $q:E\to M$ with $p$ surjective and $g_i^k q(z)=j_n(V)(p(z))x_i$ for every $i<t$ and $z\in E$.

source.place: Lemma 01PM (lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact-open-in-affine), proof, denominator construction; Lemma 01PQ (lemma-sections-over-quasi-compact-open), affine reduction. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PM and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PQ.

proof.text: Use the recorded affine-power helper to obtain quasi-coherence of P_n and image(j_n(V))=J^n, with J=span(g_i).

Induct on t to show J^(t*k+1) is contained in H=span(g_i^k). For t=0 it is the zero ideal. Split the first generator from the rest, and use (A+B)^(k+(t*k+1)) <= A^k+B^(t*k+1). The singleton power equals span(g_0^k), and the induction bound handles the remaining generators. These are Mathlib Ideal.sup_pow_add_le_pow_sup_pow and Ideal.span_singleton_pow, with elementary ideal inclusions.

Define E as the submodule of P_n(V) times M consisting of pairs (b,m) such that g_i^k*m=j_n(b)*x_i for all i. The two projections are linear. Induction on membership in H proves that every r in H has an m satisfying these equations: for a generator g_l^k use x_l and the compatibility hypothesis; use zero, addition, and scalar multiplication for the other cases. Since j_n(b) lies in H, the first projection is surjective. The second projection satisfies the displayed scalar identity by the definition of E. This construction also handles t=0, k=0, a unit ideal, and the zero ring.

theorem ideal_power_numerator_presentation
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {I : X.Modules}
    (ι : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) [Mono ι] [I.IsQuasicoherent]
    (F : X.Modules) (V : X.affineOpens) (t k : ℕ)
    (g : Fin t → Γ(X, V.1)) (x : Fin t → Γ(F, V.1))
    (hg : (LinearMap.range (ι.val.app (op V.1)).hom : Ideal Γ(X, V.1)) =
      Ideal.span (Set.range g))
    (hx : ∀ i j, g j ^ k • x i = g i ^ k • x j) :
    let n := t * k + 1
    ((idealSheafPower ι n).1).IsQuasicoherent ∧
    (LinearMap.range ((idealSheafPower ι n).2.val.app (op V.1)).hom :
      Ideal Γ(X, V.1)) ≤ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦ g i ^ k)) ∧
    ∃ (E : ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, V.1))
      (p : E →ₗ[Γ(X, V.1)] Γ((idealSheafPower ι n).1, V.1))
      (q : E →ₗ[Γ(X, V.1)] Γ(F, V.1)),
      Function.Surjective p ∧ ∀ (i : Fin t) (z : E),
        g i ^ k • q z =
          (show Γ(X, V.1) from (idealSheafPower ι n).2.app V.1 (p z)) • x i
